summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with primary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a suprapubic catheter, was admitted with a catheter-associated urinary tract infection presenting with high fever, tachycardia, and malaise. He was initially treated with IV vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam. Urine cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa; due to intermediate sensitivity of Pseudomonas to ciprofloxacin, he was transitioned to high-dose oral ciprofloxacin for a 14-day course per infectious disease guidance. His symptoms resolved, and labs normalized. A suprapubic catheter exchange was performed during admission. He improved to baseline motor function and was discharged home with follow-up arranged in urology and instructions to monitor for recurrence.
